articles.title: Vitamin B3 Shows 82% Progression-Free Rate in Glioblastoma — Will Oncology's Profit Machine Let This Through?
articles.summary: A small but striking trial found that high-dose niacin kept 82% of glioblastoma patients progression-free at six months by reactivating immune cells suppressed by the tumor microenvironment. Glioblastoma kills nearly everyone within 15 months under standard of care, yet this cheap, off-patent vitamin has received no major pharma backing. The question is whether a non-patentable metabolic intervention will ever get the Phase III funding it deserves.

articles.title: Repurposed Drugs Like Ivermectin Could Upend Cancer Care — And That's Exactly Why You Haven't Heard About Them
articles.summary: Dr. William Makis argues that cheap, off-patent drugs including ivermectin demonstrate measurable anticancer activity that the profit-driven oncology establishment has systematically ignored. These drugs cannot be patented, meaning there is no financial incentive for Big Pharma to fund trials, leaving patients abandoned to expensive standard-of-care regimens with dismal survival rates. The suppression is not accidental — it is structural.

articles.title: Antidepressants: The Benefits vs. Harms Debate Medicine Refuses to Have Honestly
articles.summary: A detailed examination of antidepressant pharmacology surfaces what psychiatry's mainstream journals have long soft-pedaled: the gap between marketed efficacy and real-world benefit is substantial, and the harm profile — dependence, withdrawal, emotional blunting, sexual dysfunction — is routinely minimized in prescribing discussions. With antidepressant prescriptions at record highs globally, the cost of this institutional dishesty is measured in millions of damaged lives. The field's reluctance to conduct rigorous, independent long-term safety reviews is itself a form of censorship.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Hid iLet Device Safety Problems From Investors — FDA Compliance Failures Now Trigger Fraud Lawsuit
articles.summary: Beta Bionics allegedly misled investors about the safety and commercial viability of its iLet automated insulin delivery device while concealing FDA compliance failures, triggering a 37% stock collapse and a securities fraud class action. This is textbook medical device regulatory capture in reverse: a company that gamed the FDA approval process is now exposed not by regulators but by market losses. Patients who used the device deserve answers the company clearly never intended to provide.

articles.title: Independence Blue Cross Pocketed $22.5M in Fraudulent Medicare Advantage Overpayments — And Took Years to Get Caught

Regulators treated this as a civil settlement rather than criminal fraud, meaning no executives face prosecution. The fine is a rounding error against the profits extracted.

Metformin costs pennies per dose and cannot be patented, which explains why large-scale human longevity trials remain chronically underfunded despite compelling data. The TAME trial is the exception — and it took a decade of advocacy just to get it launched.
